compiled_state.title: Test creation calibration (a): generation-time prevention of change-detector tests
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
## Context

LLM test-writing sub-agents in this project (red-test-writer, sprint task-execution prompt, fix-bug RED phase) routinely produce tests that assert on internal method names, mock-invocation counts, or source-grep patterns rather than on observable system behavior. Research documents this failure mode: ~25% of LLM oracles are wrong-but-confident (Di Grazia et al. ASE 2025), 30-60% of LLM tests fail basic compile/execute floors (Yuan et al. 2024), and LLM tests show Assertion Roulette in 38-49% of class-level tests (Wang et al. 2024). The existing 5-rule behavioral-testing-standard.md describes correct principles but is too abstract to bind at generation time. This epic introduces a structured per-test intent-claim header that test-writers attach to every new or modified test, and extends the existing code-reviewer-test-quality agent with two review dimensions to enforce both assertion shape and articulation during code review. Pre-commit gating is deliberately out of scope — enforcement runs through the review overlay only, with iteration in the wild before any deterministic tooling is added.

## Success Criteria

- SC1: plugins/dso/skills/shared/prompts/behavioral-testing-standard.md gains Rule 6 — every NEW or MODIFIED test in the diff carries a fenced "## Test Intent" header above the test function with fields intent_id (SC|DoD|AC reference from parent ticket subtree, or "UNTRACKED — <one-line rationale>" permitted sentinel) and catches_regression_where (sentence-completion form: "this test turns RED if and only if [specific production-code change]"). Rule 6 includes canonical per-language header fixture examples covering Python (docstring with markdown fence inside), JavaScript/TypeScript (block comment with markdown fence inside), and bash (line-comment block with markdown fence inside). Legacy tests not modified in the diff are exempt.

- SC2: behavioral-testing-standard.md gains Rule 7 — when adding behavioral coverage for an intent_id already claimed by an existing test, add a sibling parameterized case or new sibling test function in the same test file. Do NOT append assertions to an existing test function. Do NOT create a duplicate test function claiming the same intent_id without an orthogonal scenario suffix. Each test function carries at most one "## Test Intent" header. behavioral-testing-standard.md is designated a safeguard file per CLAUDE.md rule 22 — sub-agents may not propose edits that weaken Rule 6 or 7 without explicit user approval.

- SC3: Three test-writing surfaces updated to reference Rules 6 and 7 in their generation guidance: plugins/dso/agents/red-test-writer.md, plugins/dso/skills/sprint/prompts/task-execution.md, and the fix-bug RED-phase prompt (concrete path under plugins/dso/skills/fix-bug/ resolved during implementation-plan). Synthetic verification: a dispatch of dso:red-test-writer against a fixture task containing one AC produces a test file whose header parses under the per-language syntax appendix and whose intent_id field exactly matches the fixture AC identifier; parse success is confirmed by an automated grep that finds the fenced "## Test Intent" block, the intent_id field, and the catches_regression_where field in the output.

- SC4: plugins/dso/docs/workflows/prompts/reviewer-delta-test-quality.md (the build source for the compiled plugins/dso/agents/code-reviewer-test-quality.md agent, regenerated via build-review-agents.sh) gains two new review dimensions. Tier 1 (assertion shape) emits a finding when a test assertion targets internal method names, private state, mock-invocation counts (e.g., mock.called_with), or source-grep patterns against source files; requires assertions to target observable outputs (return values, exit codes, file contents, side effects, emitted events). Tier 2 (articulation) emits a finding when (a) a new/modified test has missing or malformed header, (b) catches_regression_where is tautological, (c) the assertions do not exercise the intent named in intent_id (REQUIRED scaffold: reviewer first lists the observable artifact each assert measures, then lists what intent_id claims is measured, then flags if these two sets are disjoint), (d) catches_regression_where would not in fact cause the test to fail given the assertions present, (e) duplicate intent_id without orthogonal scenario suffix or sibling-case structure per Rule 7. Dimension carries an anti-sycophancy prime: "Identify the single most damaging flaw. If no flaw exists, state 'No findings' explicitly." The build pipeline regenerates code-reviewer-test-quality.md from this delta source as part of the implementation work.

- SC5: A /dso:review run against a synthetic diff containing (a) a new test with no header, (b) a new test asserting only on mock.called_with(...), (c) a new test whose intent_id claims SC-1 but whose only assertion is `assert True == True`, produces a reviewer-findings.json where the findings[] array includes at least one entry with dimension matching "Tier 1 (assertion shape)" or "Tier 2 (articulation)" AND whose source_path:source_line falls inside violations (a), (b), (c) respectively. The same findings[] array contains zero entries with those dimensions whose source_line falls inside any unmodified legacy test block in the same diff.

- SC6: Pointer/version updates for the consumer files explicitly known to reference the behavioral testing standard or its Rule 5 ordinal:
  - plugins/dso/skills/implementation-plan/SKILL.md
  - plugins/dso/skills/implementation-plan/docs/reviewers/plan/tdd.md
  - plugins/dso/skills/preplanning/SKILL.md
  - plugins/dso/docs/workflows/prompts/review-fix-dispatch.md
  - plugins/dso/agents/red-test-evaluator.md (plus: rejection criteria extended to require Rule 6 header on new test output)
  - plugins/dso/skills/fix-bug/SKILL.md (the "Apply all five rules" enumeration)
  - plugins/dso/docs/AGENTS.md (the "detects 5 test bloat patterns" count)
  - tests/hooks/test-behavioral-testing-standard-rule5.sh (preamble-count assertion made version-agnostic, or removed in favor of the existing test_rule_count_matches_headings assertion which uses -ge 5)
  - tests/scripts/test-red-test-writer-md-rule5-compliance.sh (heading assertion made version-agnostic or extended)
  - tests/hooks/test-agent-standard-reference.sh (heading assertion made version-agnostic or extended)

  Each "5-rule" / "five rules" / "Rule 5" reference is updated to version-agnostic phrasing OR extended to enumerate Rules 6 and 7.

- SC7 (dogfood): The tests written for d566's own implementation carry valid Rule 6 headers. A /dso:review run on the d566 implementation PR emits zero Tier 1 or Tier 2 findings on those tests.

- SC8 (explicit descope): plugins/dso/hooks/pre-commit-test-quality-gate.sh and plugins/dso/hooks/semgrep-rules/test-anti-patterns.yaml are explicitly NOT extended by this epic. Rule 6 + Rule 7 enforcement is review-only via the dimensions added to code-reviewer-test-quality in SC4. If future evidence supports adding hook-level enforcement, a follow-on epic will scope it.

- SC9 (structural sweep): During implementation, the implementer runs the following case-insensitive grep across plugins/, tests/, and docs/ (file types: *.md, *.sh, *.py, *.yaml, *.yml):

  ```
  grep -rEni '5[-. ]?rule|five[-. ]?rules?|Rule[[:space:]]+5\b|behavioral[-. _]testing[-. _]standard'
  ```

  Every match is triaged into one of three outcomes: (i) updated to version-agnostic phrasing or extended to reference Rules 6/7, (ii) explicitly descoped with a one-line rationale (e.g., "Rule 5 in this context refers to a different standard"), or (iii) already version-agnostic — no change required. The implementation PR description includes the full final grep output (count and list of matches) plus the triage disposition for each one (file path → outcome i/ii/iii with rationale where required). Pattern validation against the 14 consumers identified during brainstorm confirmed 100% coverage at brainstorm time; this SC ensures any consumer added between brainstorm and implementation is also caught.

## Approach

Inline rule additions to behavioral-testing-standard.md (Rule 6 + Rule 7 + per-language syntax appendix with canonical fixture examples). Prompt updates to three test-writing surfaces. Extension of reviewer-delta-test-quality.md (build source) — rebuild via build-review-agents.sh regenerates code-reviewer-test-quality.md. Pointer updates across the 10 named consumer files in SC6, plus structural sweep per SC9 to catch any unenumerated consumers. No new tooling, no new contracts, no new scripts.

## Scenario Analysis

- Fabricated tautological catches_regression_where (high/correctness): partially mitigated by Tier 2(b) and (d) reviewer checks; residual risk that the reviewer is itself LLM-judgment-based.
- intent_id collision across distinct scenarios sharing an abstract SC (high/correctness): partially mitigated by Rule 7 orthogonal-suffix requirement; "orthogonal" is reviewer judgment.
- Claim-vs-assertion contradiction degrades without manifest (critical/observability): partially mitigated by predicate-listing scaffold in Tier 2(c); semantic drift remains until 94ed-f55c manifest ships.
- Bash test header silent no-match in parser (high/runtime): partially mitigated by canonical per-language fixtures in SC1.
- LLM reviewer sycophancy on fluent headers (high/correctness): partially mitigated by anti-sycophancy prime; instructional primes are a known weak defense.
- Test rename orphans header (medium/configuration): unmitigated; deferred to 94ed/411b.
- Multiple tasks retroactively claim same test for different intent_ids (high/correctness): mitigated by one-header-per-function rule in SC2.
- Agent self-proposes Rule 6 relaxation (medium/configuration): mitigated by safeguard-file designation in SC2.
- Polyglot header embedding inconsistency (medium/runtime): partially mitigated by canonical fixtures.

## Research Findings

Three independent research dispatches during brainstorm surveyed academic literature, open-source tooling, and practitioner thought leaders on the question "at generation time, how do we know whether a candidate test would catch a real regression?" Convergent findings across all streams identified three signal tiers: Tier 1 (assertion shape — observable output vs internal name; cheap floor; 30–60% of LLM tests fail this per Yuan et al. 2024), Tier 2 (articulation — name the invariant and the plausible mutation; medium cost, LLM-friendly; cross-practitioner consensus from Khorikov, Beck, Bach/Bolton, Hughes/Wayne, Fowler), Tier 3 (empirical — mutant kill on the changed line; Meta TestGen-LLM 2025 mutation-guided pipeline; deferred to sibling epic 411b-a047). This epic implements Tiers 1 and 2 only.

## Dependencies

- a03c-d55e (Closure Checks schema migration) — required because intent_id under Rule 6 must reference end-state SC/DoD/AC, which a03c structurally separates from transitional Closure Checks via the new "## Closure Checks" template section and the updated verifiable-sc-check.md end-state-only rule. d566 owns the header schema; a03c's completion-verifier consumes Rule 6 headers for intent_id→test_artifact lookup. Sequential dependency, no conflict.
- 94ed-f55c (Plan-time intent allocation manifest) — required because Rule 6 intent_id field references manifest entries. d566 ships only after 94ed publishes the manifest schema and intent_id format.
- 7f42-e41f (suite growth metrics, sibling) — sequencing: d566 ships first; 7f42 builds on d566's header schema for its per-intent-item growth metrics. To avoid concurrent edits to behavioral-testing-standard.md, 7f42's brainstorm/implementation defers until d566 closes.

## Sibling Calibration Program

- 7f42-e41f: suite growth tracks behavioral coverage (Tier 1+2 metrics).
- 69e8-af39: feedback loop from production bugs and review findings into test-creation prompts.
- 411b-a047: mutation-testing infrastructure (Tier 3 empirical verification).

## Planning Intelligence Log

- Web research (Step 2 of scrutiny pipeline): not triggered — external research was performed at user request during Phase 1 dialogue, prior to Step 2 firing.
- Scenario analysis (Step 3): triggered (SCs ≥ 5); 12 red-team scenarios surfaced, 9 surviving after blue-team filter.
- Cross-epic scan (Step 2.25): triggered against a focused candidate set of 16 test/agent/review-related open epics. 1 ambiguity (a03c-d55e) resolved in Dependencies; 4 consideration signals on sibling/prereq epics; 1 benign signal on kudos.
- Bot-psychologist (Step 5): triggered (LLM-instruction signal: agent definitions + prompt templates). Findings folded into SC1, SC2, SC4 (catches_regression_where rename, UNTRACKED sentinel, predicate-listing scaffold, anti-sycophancy prime, sibling-case rule).
- Fidelity review (Step 4): Agent Clarity pass (5, 4), Value pass (4, 4), Scope (4, 4, 4, 3); consumer_completeness=3 finding structurally resolved by SC9 sweep. Reviewer anti-pattern incident filed as bug 270e-225f-6c72-4f0c.
- Scale context (Step 0): not applicable — development-time tool, per-test-author invocation.
- Session-signal override for complexity routing: success_criteria_count = 9 (≥ 7 threshold) AND scenario_survivor_count = 9 (close to 10 threshold) — routes to /dso:preplanning full mode.

comments.body: SPEC AMENDMENT from 94ed-f55c-51f5-45f6 brainstorm: 94ed defines intent_id format as STABLE slug (regex [a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+){2,5}) minted at item creation — not ordinal references like SC-1 or DoD-2.a. d566's Rule 6 (in behavioral-testing-standard.md) was originally drafted assuming ordinal references; this amendment updates Rule 6 to consume stable slug intent_ids from 94ed's manifest. Recoverable since d566 has not yet been preplanned or implemented. When d566 enters preplanning, update Rule 6's intent_id field description and accept/reject examples to use stable slug format.
